name: Pine Needle
lede: Pine Needle is ColorHub's English name for Matsuba-iro, a muted olive green that Japanese tradition names directly for pine needles, and the same hue was independently catalogued by Maerz and Paul in 1930.

sections.title: A literal pine-needle green
sections.body:
Wikipedia's list of traditional Japanese colors gives this swatch as Matsuba-iro (松葉色), literally "pine needle color" [1]. The same shade was independently catalogued by Maerz and Paul in their 1930 *Dictionary of Color*, later cited by NBS Circular 553 in 1955 [2]. The ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955 places it in block 127, "grayish olive green," about 3.9 units from that block's centre [2]. The library's nearest other named color is [[rifle-green]], 2.6 units away [2].

Measured in LCH it reads lightness 31, chroma 17, hue 120 degrees, a dark, moderately saturated olive green, darker than most garden pine foliage appears to the eye [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match in 934 of 23,781 paintings, about 4 percent, as photographed [3]. It splits almost evenly between mid-tone and shadow roles, 46 and 47 percent, and is rarely a highlight [3]. Henri Rousseau carries it at nearly 12 times the archive's overall rate, fitting his jungle-foliage canvases [3]. It shares canvases more than chance with the color words Hunter Green and [[olive]], and its presence peaks in the 1920s, in 24 of 237 paintings [3].
